question: ACE inhibitors and ARBs are absolutely contraindicated throughout all three trimesters of pregnancy because they cause fetal renal tubular dysplasia and oligohydramnios.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is true. ACEi and ARBs are absolutely contraindicated in pregnancy (all trimesters). They impair fetal kidney development by blocking angiotensin II-dependent nephrogenesis, leading to oligohydramnios and fetal renal failure — a class-specific teratogenic hazard that also applies to ARBs.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. RAAS blockade impairs fetal renal development — angiotensin II is critical for normal nephrogenesis. Exposure in the 2nd and 3rd trimesters causes fetal renal failure, oligohydramnios, limb contractures, pulmonary hypoplasia, and death. 1st trimester use is also associated with cardiovascular malformations. Both ACEi and ARBs carry the same teratogenic risk.
